body.error_description: The request requires higher privileges than provided by the access token.

source.note: The page's only insufficient-scope example is for a request that needs `sudo`: status 403 with {"error":"insufficient_scope","error_description":"The request requires higher privileges than provided by the access token.","scope":"sudo"}. Adapted to `GET /user` sent with a token holding only `read_repository` + `write_repository`, whose scopes the access-token-scopes page (https://docs.gitlab.com/security/tokens/access_token_scopes/) describes as Git-only; the `scope` value is this corpus's guess at the scopes `/user` accepts (`read_user` grants it, per that page). NOT measured on gitlab.com — docs/TODO.md's WP-141 row. WP-141's scope proof reads the status and the `error` identifier only.

"Retrieve the current user" example response, as `merge-request-adoption.json` already uses it, for a fake operator whose run token was created with an API scope — the token WP-141's scope proof refuses because the read succeeded.

The status table: "401 Unauthorized - The user isn't authenticated. A valid user token is necessary." The body is the shape this corpus's other GitLab errors carry; WP-141's scope proof reads only the status.

A 403 that is NOT a refusal for scope. The status table documents "403 Forbidden - The request isn't allowed"; the body (no `error`) is this corpus's guess at what a proxy, a web application firewall in front of gitlab.com or a terms-of-service block answers — not a recording. It holds WP-141 review round 1's rule: only `error: insufficient_scope` proves a repository-only token.

The "List protected branches" response shape (the single-branch example's members, as an array), with this corpus's rules: `main` push No one; `release` exact No one but the wildcard `rel*` admitting Maintainers — GitLab applies the most permissive matching rule (https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/repository/branches/protected/), so `release` is pushable; `stable` exact No one with force push off, but the wildcard `st*` (also No one) allows force push — the most permissive matching rule wins, so `stable` admits a force push; `*-hotfix` a wildcard admitting force push, matching nothing the suite reads but `main-hotfix`. `develop` matches no rule (unprotected). No `x-next-page`: one page.
